where: Section 2 and the figure note and Worked example 1 (steps 5 and 9) and Quiz Q5
problem: Legacy software is listed as an application domain and the payroll systems are said to fall 'under legacy, not under application software'. Legacy is a status (old, still in production, still business-critical), not a domain: a payroll system is application software that happens to be legacy. A student who copies this exclusive classification into an exam answer is marked wrong, because domains in the standard lists do not include legacy at all.
fix: Keep the domain list to the seven standard domains (system, application, engineering/scientific, embedded, product-line/reuse, web and mobile, AI) and present legacy separately as a status that cuts across domains. In the worked example, classify the 2 payroll systems as application software that is also legacy, and keep the total at 40. Change the figure note to 'the two old payroll systems are application software that has become legacy'. Quiz Q2's acceptable list should then offer the seven domains.

problem: The myth 'a general statement of the objective is enough to start coding' is put under the management group. Standard textbook groupings place it under customer myths ('a general statement of objectives is sufficient to begin writing programs; we can fill in the details later'). A student reproducing the table by group loses marks.
fix: Move that row to the customer group, keeping the correction. Management myths then read: adding programmers catches up a late project; we already have a book of standards and procedures, so quality is covered. Six rows can still be kept (2 management, 2 customer, 2 practitioner).

where: Section 2, application domain list, application software bullet
problem: The bullet says 'Web and mobile apps are the largest modern sub-class' of application software, while the next-but-one bullet lists 'web and mobile applications' as a separate domain. A student cannot tell which domain a web app belongs to.
fix: State it once explicitly: 'Web and mobile apps are treated here as a separate domain; some texts count them as a sub-class of application software. Either answer is accepted, but be consistent.' Then adjust the bullets.

where: Section 2, four shapes of software, software as a service
problem: 'the customer pays a subscription and uses the vendor's running system, like a GST filing portal billed per return' mixes a subscription model with per-use billing, so the defining feature of SaaS reads unclearly.
fix: Write: 'the customer pays a recurring fee and uses the vendor's running system, for example a GST filing portal. The fee may be a flat subscription or billed per use.'
